newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FORECAST-Lisbon stocks seen with more 1996 upside.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Lisbon stocks seen with more 1996 upside.

text.p: Portuguese shares could gain a further four or five percent over the last quarter of the year, buoyed by the expected easy passage of a deficit-cutting budget, lower interest rates and the prospects of greater economic growth in Europe in 1997, analysts said.
"The market has room to gain four or five percent,", said analyst Jose Freire of brokers Eser.
"We think the index (PSI20) can close above 5,000 points, which would mean a further rise of at least 5.2 percent," said Joao Vermelho of Central de Investimentos (CI).
Since the beginning of the year the index of 20 leading blue chips, which is used for the futures contract, has risen 23 percent to 4,774.67.
"Everybody is going to bet on a faster rate of growth in Europe and that is good for our companies that export," said Freire.

Vermelho said that an index at 5,000 would translate into an average price-earnings ratio of 13.8, a price to cashflow of 4.9 and a dividend yield of 3.3 percent which was "still pretty reasonable" when compared with other European markets.
This points to a "well-behaved market in 1997," he added.
Carlos Peixoto of Ascor said he expected to see some return to the market by small investors due to its good performance.

Analysts said that the feeling that inflation was declining and growing confidence that Portugal can meet its 1997 budget deficit target of 2.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) suggested a steady narrowing in interest differentials with major European countries.
Jose Freire said that the banks could be given a boost by third quarter results, due around the end of October, which were expected to be good even if the profit came mostly from trading.
With regard to Portugal Telecom (PT), the bourse's most liquid stock, analysts saw little volatility as international attention would be focused on Deutsche Telecom (DT).
"Attention is focused on DT and for this reason there is not much room for PT to fluctuate", he said.
Carlos Peixoto saw upside for cement company Cimpor following the second phase of its privatisation which will be completed on October 15.
